 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 11.01.2016 passed in MVC.No.3841/2012 by the VII Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT-3, Bengaluru, praying for modification of the aforesaid judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

entities.text: VII Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT-3, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the driver of the Tata Sumo was not at all rash and negligent, but the driver of the KSRTC was rash and negligent.

Therefore,
submitted that the entire rashness and negligence may be fastened on the driver of the KSRTC.
Therefore, prays to allow the appeal by modifying the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimant justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. In the present case, the manner of accident is that the claimant was riding the motor cycle and it was dashed by Tata Sumo as the driver of Tata Suma was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and due to which, the claimant fell on the road and at the same time, KSRTC bus driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant, due to which, the claimant had sustained grievous injuries.
7. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances and scenario of the accident revealed on the record and appreciating the evidence on record, the claimant was first hit by Tata Sumo vehicle.
If the claimant was not dashed by Tata Sumo, then the claimant could not have fallen on the ground and the accident could have been avoided.

But the driver of the Tata Sumo had dashed the motor cycle of the claimant, due to which, the claimant was NC: 2023:KHC:21213 constrained to fell on the ground, then the KSRTC bus had hit the claimant.

8. Therefore, considering these aspects, the Tribunal is justified in holding that the driver of Tata Sumo has contributed 50% of rashness and negligence and the driver of the KSRTC had contributed 50% of rashness and negligence.
Therefore, it is proved that both the drivers have equally contributed to the accident and it is correctly held by the Tribunal.

Therefore, no good ground is The United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sri. Kumar on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181564331/
3 made out to cause interference with the findings given by the Tribunal.
